title: Job 18
paragraphs: ¹ Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said: ² "How long before you stop making speeches? Think carefully, and then we will speak. ³ Why do you treat us as animals — as stupid in your eyes? ⁴ You who tear yourself apart in your anger — shall the earth be abandoned for your sake? Shall rocks be moved from their place?

⁶ The light in his tent will grow dark, and the lamp beside him will be snuffed out. ⁷ His strong stride will falter, and his own schemes will bring him down. ⁸ His own feet throw him into a net; he walks right into the trap. ⁹ A snare catches him by the heel and holds him fast. ¹⁰ A noose is hidden in the ground for him, a trap lies across his path.

¹¹ Terrors beset him on every side and chase him at every step. ¹² Calamity is hungry for him, and disaster stands ready at his side. ¹³ Disease devours his skin; death's firstborn eats away his limbs. ¹⁴ He is torn from the security he trusted in and marched off to the king of terrors.

¹⁶ His roots will wither below, and his branches be cut off above. ¹⁷ His memory will vanish from the earth; no one will know his name in the streets. ¹⁸ He will be driven from light into darkness, chased out of the world. ¹⁹ He will leave no child, no descendant among his people, no survivor in the places where he lived. ²⁰ Those in the west will be appalled at his fate, and those in the east will be seized with horror.
²¹ Surely these are the dwellings of the wicked — this is the place of those who do not know God.
